blocking_findings.title: New readback/cell/repetition mechanisms still admit false marker and depth proof
evidence: reflection of actual Java measure: unrelated expected pattern passes; mirrored yellow depth failure ignored by first passing orientation
blocking_findings.details: Density/position and direct rearm arithmetic are repaired. Separate pass-cell command cannot prove rejected-box command issuance. Python trusts sparse/defaulted aggregate data. Every-240 sampling misses intermediate failures; every-600 evidence persistence can hide late sampled failures. Retained marker report is frame 4800/20 clean while final checkpoint is 5161 and log contains 22 samples. Harness metadata lacks frame/submission binding.

blocking_findings.title: Immediate shutdown can destroy a marker on a device whose completion was not observed
blocking_findings.details: Specific fence/drain/destroy/missing-device/retirement repairs are confirmed. If the MC device is replaced, adopted context remains A while current marker follows B; release waits A and destroys B without identity validation. Public waitIdle also still drains pending frees after unchecked wait, though no production caller was found. Source-path finding, not an observed hardware crash.

non_blocking_findings.title: Failure leaks are not uniformly bounded or reported
non_blocking_findings.details: Close failures are swallowed; continued periodic readbacks can abandon up to 40 MiB each attempt. Retirement leaks can recur over unlimited lifecycle/format changes. NOTES deduplicates/caps messages, not objects/bytes. One-shot compute/adoption/shader leaks are session-bounded; healthy callbacks do close buffers.
